adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the target calendar with:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

(and similarly for `calendarId` in `deleteEvent`). When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`null`/`undefined`), the `.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares `externalId` to `null/undefined` and will almost always return `undefined`, making this fallback effectively dead code. Prior code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` directly as the fallback.

This means legacy references lacking `externalCalendarId` will not select any destination calendar id from `event.destinationCalendar` and may call Google APIs with `calendarId: undefined` (or at least fail to target the intended destination calendar). The diff also shows `deleteEvent` now derives `calendarId` the same way, so the same issue applies there; whether it still falls back to `primary` at the API call site is not shown in the diff, but the destination-calendar fallback is clearly broken.
